DEPARTMENT OF ECOLOGY

DANIEL J. EVANS
GOVERNOR

DIRECTOR
May 17, 1972
Mr. Paul T. Benson, Jr., Assistant Director
Office of Program Planning and Fiscal Management
Insurance Building
Olympia, Washington 98501
Dear Mr. Benson:
In accordance with your request of April 6, 1972, we have reviewed the draft environmental statement (DES 72 - 44) for the proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972, which was prepared by the U. S. Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife. Resolution of problems encountered by endangered species should include the adequate consideration of all components of ecosystems within which the endangered animal exists.
We feel the statement should provide further explanation of the portion which reads, "The methods employed to reach this goal will not require the irreversible or irretrievable commitment of natural resources."
The capacity of individual states to accomplish conservation of endangered species should not be diffused or diluted by this much needed and very commendable legislation. The role of the states in this capacity (under this legislation) should be more fully defined in the statement.
We realize that the overall impacts of this proposed statute cannot be completely evaluated because of its general nature—the species are not all defined, land areas required are not defined, costs of implementation are not identified, control methods are not defined. In conjunction with these generalities, our response should also be of a general nature.
In closing, we feel this proposed legislation is much needed and certainly reflects the response of the public.
Sincerely,
Jula. Hahn
Fred D. Hahn, Assistant Director
Office of Planning and Program Development
